body: QString[Literal]::arg() integral signatures no longer accept sting-ish types like char16_t, as returned by QChar::unicode(), in Qt 6.9. [1] Cast the sting-ish char16_t to quint16 to disambiguate and avoid compilation errors. [1] https://code.qt.io/cgit/qt/qtbase.git/commit/?h=6.9.0&id=563ed822f86 - - - This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/TokTok/debugtox/23)

comment_regular_data.body: @BSDKaffee The line is now too long for restyled. (check the restyled diff)

@Green-Sky Thanks for the pointer. Hopefully, all should be good now. I try to adhere to project contribution guidelines, but I didn't see one here. Kind of got lucky with the "fix:" prefix at the top of commit message, though...there is a check for that I see now too, but that was initially just intuition trying to stylize it to fit the established commit history. Had no idea that was a checked-for keyword since it wasn't used before.

No worries, the ci is in place for a reason. Slightly annoying that you have not contributed before, so we have to approve the ci everytime you push a change for now.

Looks like you added whitespace at the end of the line now.

We also require commits to be signed.
Guess it would've helped if I actually added the change to the commit. Sorry about that.

> We also require commits to be signed.

The last thing we require. You need to setup commit signing, and add the (pub) key to github.

https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/managing-commit-signature-verification/about-commit-signature-verification
The commit is now signed with my GPG key. Thank you for your patience.

commit.message:
fix: Adapt to Qt 6.9

QString[Literal]::arg() integral signatures no longer accept char16_t,
as returned by QChar::unicode(), in Qt 6.9.

Signed-off-by: Jason E. Hale <jhale@FreeBSD.org>
